dirty_scope: docs/architecture.md contained this same decision update when the receipt was written; no engine or tooling file was modified.
scope: Specify the DeepSeek-V4.1 port boundary, artifact policy, and initial backend order. This is a design decision from the pinned Lucebox source and current host inventory; it does not implement a converter, quantizer, graph, kernel, or backend.

quantization.rule: Every runnable Strata artifact for DeepSeek V4.1, and future model ports by default, must be generated by an RESMP-owned deterministic quantizer from a pinned source checkpoint.
quantization.input: The preferred initial source is deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 revision 1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170, whose transfer is already in progress on B550.
quantization.external_artifacts: Lucebox ROCMFP files and other prequantized artifacts are comparisons and format references only, not runtime dependencies.
required_outputs: Source checkpoint revision and tensor manifest
RESMP-owned quantization recipe and calibration identity
Exact inverse or bounded reconstruction check
CPU/CUDA parity gates for every consumed pack format
DSpark short-sequence parity before speculative output is trusted
Real-model quality and same-day memory/throughput controls

backend_order.selected: CUDA and CPU component extraction on B550 first
reason: B550 has two live sm_86 RTX 3090 Ti cards and no HIP runtime.
Strix also has an NVIDIA CUDA device, not an AMD APU.
Lucebox's HIP choice is a qualification and hardware-target decision, not a DeepSeek architectural requirement.
Lucebox's V4.1 CUDA refusal is an unresolved candidate-selection parity problem, not proof that CUDA cannot implement the model.
A wholesale HIP port would drag in AMD-specific ROCMFP expert formats and an external artifact contract, contrary to the RESMP-owned quantization rule.
backend_order.hip_exception: Start with HIP only if an AMD/Strix-Halo-class machine becomes the primary acceptance target, or if an unmodified Lucebox build is temporarily required as an oracle. That path still needs named hardware and parity evidence.

use_as_semantic_references: deepseek41 tensor names, metadata, and geometry
CSA2 compressed-cache sharing and hierarchical candidate selection
DSpark target capture, draft, rollback, confidence, and verification state machine
Three-tier expert ownership, protected experts, router bias, and prefetch scheduling
O_DIRECT expert and Engram streaming concepts
reimplement_for_strata: Own model graph and layout checks
Own quant formats and CUDA/CPU kernels
B550 CUDA candidate-selection path with exact parity
Own placement planner and DSpark integration
do_not_adopt: Lucebox GGUF dialect as the Strata product format
A published DSpark sidecar as the canonical build artifact
Unqualified CUDA candidate behavior that differs beyond documented ties

cuda_gate.observation: A non-HIP compile assigns unsupported = a CUDA build for V4.1; the comment says candidate-block selection past 16,384 compressed rows does not match the reference.
test_v41_indexer_candidates skips non-CPU backends when GGML_USE_HIP is absent, citing 6 of 80 mismatching queries on sm_121.
The V4.1 support table marks loader, CSA2, Engram, three expert owners, DSpark, paged serving, and prefill as implemented, while refusing CUDA builds.

portable_code_signal: deepseek4_dspark.cpp has no direct HIP conditional in the surveyed section.
deepseek4_dspark_spec.cpp uses generic ggml CUDA/HIP API names for backend copies.
moe_hybrid_expert_cache.cpp separates only a small HIP host-allocation branch from the generic CUDA API path.
The CUDA refusal is a qualification gate rather than a CMake inability to compile CUDA.

host_inventory_from_prior_probe.B550: two RTX 3090 Ti sm_86 GPUs, CUDA driver 595.99.02, no torch/vLLM/SGLang/HIP runtime
host_inventory_from_prior_probe.Strix: RTX 5070 Laptop CUDA path plus Intel CPU/NPU; no AMD GPU

first_implementation_seams: Write an RESMP-owned source-checkpoint manifest reader for DeepSeek V4.1 1017.
Define the Strata pack format before choosing bit widths; recognition of MXFP4/NVFP4 is not execution support.
Port the candidate-selection reference as a CPU test first, then implement CUDA to pass it beyond the 16,384-row boundary.
Port Engram hash and row lookup independently from any ROCMFP expert reader.
Recreate DSpark target capture and verification semantics behind Strata interfaces before optimizing.
